- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon; adjust upward for persistent upward trends.
- When the history shows a recent sharp spike, forecast should not overshoot — cap or smooth out the immediate post-spike values.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; apply dampening factor to forecast variance after high-momentum periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% to align with historical mean reversion behavior.
- Lagged response: if true outcome is higher than forecast, model often lags by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to be slightly ahead of true value in the next 1–2 periods.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values — if last 5–7 days are high, forecast should not assume continuation unless confirmed by momentum indicators.
